reason: The mechanism is real; two of the finding's load-bearing perceptual claims are measurably false, and the fix as written turns a green gate red. Driven in chromium at 1440 across full/partial/first-run. Confirmed: kpi() at lately.html:692-694 does split on `known && n > 0`; in full the row is DIV(9 lead), A(3), A(2), A(1), DIV(0) — three anchors at href='#', tabIndex 0, cursor pointer; partial is A(3), DIV(—), A(1), DIV(0); first-run inverts to one anchor among four divs, as claimed. Clicking a card or pressing Enter on it appends '#' and nothing else: scrollY 0 -> 0, focus stays on the anchor, no repaint. So far the seat is right. Refuted on the two claims the consequence actually rests on. FIRST, 'At rest the two are pixel-identical — same paper, same hairline, same 34px numeral, same meter' is wrong on the meter, and the meter is the element that decides it. Measured on a 170px track: the three anchors paint indigo #4f46e5 at 57 / 38 / 19px (scaleX 0.333 / 0.222 / 0.111); the zero card paints 0px on a zinc-300 rail (.meter i.zero, --f:0); the unavailable card in partial draws no meter at all and prints 'Not available'. The link/div split is tracked exactly by the meter in every state — an anchor always carries paint in that slot, a div never does. A filled meter does not *announce* a link role, and I am not pretending it does, but the row is not the undifferentiated wall of five identical tiles the finding describes, and the sentence 'nothing at rest to tell them apart' is false as written. SECOND, the finding credits the anchors with 'its own hover and active rules' and then builds the fix on deleting them. Measured, that transform channel is already dead: .rise (:485) is `animation: rise 0.5s var(--ease) both` and @keyframes rise (:480) ends `to { transform: none }`, so the filled animation value outranks every normal declaration and pins transform on all five cards forever. Rest, hover and mouse-down all read matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0) — a.kpi:hover's translateY(-2px) and a.kpi:active never paint. The only live hover signal on a KPI card is border-top-color shifting from rgba(17,17,17,0.055) to rgba(17,17,17,0.1), a hairline alpha step. This is the same cascade class that kept 'Best week · 8' unpainted through r1, and interaction-check.mjs:1318 cannot see it because `has('a.kpi:active')` tests only that the selector exists in a stylesheet, never that it renders. THIRD, and decisive under this file's rule that a correct problem with a wrong fix is refuted: dropping the anchor branch as proposed makes `has('a.kpi:active')` false, so interaction-check.mjs:1325 'every control acknowledges a press' fails and the behaviour gate goes 365/366. The engagement's exit condition is both gates green; a fix that ships a red gate is not the fix. It also leaves interaction-check.mjs:311-315 ('a true zero draws its meter and is not a link to an empty list') vacuously true, quietly deleting the only assertion that guards the policy the fix is trying to install. Severity holds at the seat's 'defect' — the surface offers a role it does not honour, but every word on it stays true and the row still reads correctly as five figures over one denominator; nothing here is blocking or misleading. The corrected fix is in sharpenedFix and is worth taking.
sharpenedFix:
Keep the direction — the hero's decision applies to the row — but land it in three parts, not one. (1) lately.html:692-694: drop the branch, always return `
${body}
`. Delete a.kpi:hover, a.kpi:focus-visible and a.kpi:active (:323-325), noting in the comment that two of the three were already dead in transform so only the border-alpha hover is actually being removed. (2) interaction-check.mjs, same commit or the gate goes red: remove `kpi: has('a.kpi:active')` from the press roster at :1318 and from the assertion at :1325 — .btn and .dot carry no .rise class (verified: document.querySelector('.dot.rise') and '.btn.rise' are both null), so their press states are live and that assertion stays meaningful for them. Then replace the now-vacuous :311-315 zero-card check with a positive one that guards the new policy across all seven states: no element matching .kpi is an A, none has tabIndex >= 0, and none carries role='link'. (3) Separately, fix the cascade bug this exposed, because it is what hid the dead press state from the gate for a whole round: .rise (:485) fills `both` over a keyframe ending `transform: none`, which pins transform above all normal declarations on .card.hero, .kpi.lead, .kpi, .card.ages, .limit and figure.ghost — any future :hover or :active transform on any of those is dead on arrival. Change .rise to `animation: rise 0.5s var(--ease) backwards` so the settled element falls back to its base transform, and add a gate assertion that measures a painted transform under hover rather than testing for the selector's existence. Record the filtered-list destination on the port packet beside the hero's, so the affordance ships when the destination does.
breaks: Part 1 removes the row's three tab stops — currently the first two focus stops on the surface at 1440 — so re-measure the keyboard path end to end and confirm nothing downstream depended on a .kpi focus target; the .sr sentence in each card is read in flow and is unaffected. It also removes the only pointer feedback in the KPI row, so re-run the coarse-pointer press check from r1's no-pressed-state-anywhere and confirm the remaining .btn and .dot channels still satisfy it with the .kpi term struck. Part 2 changes two live assertions; re-run interaction-check.mjs in full and confirm the count moves deliberately rather than dropping — the zero-card assertion should be replaced, not deleted. Part 3 is the risky one: switching .rise from `both` to `backwards` unpins transform on six element classes, which will let previously-dead hover and active rules elsewhere start painting and can change settled screenshots. Re-shoot all ten frames and diff, re-run audit.mjs for motion and the settled/[data-motion="settled"] path, and check the entrance still holds its from-state before start on hero, kpi row, ages card, limit rows and the ghost figure at 390/768/1280/1440.
